A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COMFORT study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A and B are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine VLMs on COMFORT-BALL and COMFORT-CAR, including robustness, perspective-taking, and multilingual results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, including GPT-4o results across 109 languages and detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The COMFORT framework, scene-generation procedure, spatial queries, probability processing, and evaluation components remain unchanged. Added citations around probability measurement do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COMFORT-BALL, COMFORT-CAR, and the evaluation of 109 languages across 170 regions. Table 10 corrects language names for existing codes, without changing the represented coverage.

E2.justification: The same nine VLMs and the Random and Always Yes comparators remain in their corresponding comparisons. Table 2 expands mBLIP to mBLIP-BLOOMZ, already identified in Section 4 of v1.

E3.justification: Both versions report 720 English COMFORT-BALL cases and 57,600 COMFORT-CAR cases, with unchanged prompts, metrics, scene variations, and model configurations. Multilingual evaluation still uses the four canonical directions with unspecified-perspective prompts.

E4.justification: The scene-variation robustness tests, object-hallucination analysis, perspective-taking comparisons, and appendix probability-curve analyses are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: The Random comparator still reports 30 trials, and reporting of variation across scene configurations is unchanged. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results, rankings, and plotted curves are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Table 10 changes the names attached to zh from Yoruba to Chinese and zu from Chinese to Zulu, while preserving the language codes and every associated score.

T1.justification: The formal task definition, hemisphere and cosine references, and robustness and consistency equations in Section 3 remain unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contribution and findings: COMFORT evaluates spatial ambiguity, and VLMs exhibit weak robustness, limited flexibility across reference frames, and English-dominated multilingual conventions.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the same explanations involving reporting bias and translated training data, along with the same limitations concerning acceptance regions, spatial relations, occlusion, pragmatics, and machine-translated prompts. Figure 8's revised caption clarifies an already established model-based interpretation.

D1.justification: Blender scene-generation details, prompt templates, translation and back-translation procedures, language exclusions, and the project link remain unchanged. No new implementation settings or resource-access information are disclosed.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, supporting spatial-reasoning background, probability-based evaluation, 3D perception, and multilingual representations. These include Hu and Levy (2023) and Wang and Shi (2025) in Section 3.4; the overall novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and grammar edits, substitutes sagittal/lateral terminology, corrects GPT-4 to GPT-4o in Section 5.1, and updates publication headers and acknowledgments. The section organization and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 8's caption explicitly identifies GPT-4o's preferences, and Tables 2 and 10 receive model/language label corrections. Figures, plotted data, and table structures are retained, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting precision by correcting Table 10's Chinese/Zulu labels, identifying GPT-4o explicitly in Figure 8 and Section 5.1, and adding relevant references. These changes reduce potential misreading, while the methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, making the overall improvement limited.
